author: Cristian Sylvestre / David Pope
description: Much of what is “new” in safety has not been proven to make any difference to safety performance, some of it possibly making it worse. This will be new information to many. We know disruptive thinking challenges long-held beliefs and accepted norms. As such, it could be confronting for some. However, significant improvements tend to come from new perspectives and that is what we are interested in.We do not advocate one approach over another, we are here to explore new safety frontiers, to ensure that we are using everything available to help people with safety.

title: Loving Flat
author: Rochelle Moulton Lewis
description:
My breast cancer diagnosis knocked me sideways. It was an exhausting sprint to navigate a life-changing series of decisions as quickly as possible to keep the cancer from spreading. 
Aesthetic flat closure became my first choice because I wanted to maintain full range of motion in my body, I didn’t want to introduce foreign objects into my system, and most of all, I wanted to live my life vs. spinning the surgical roulette wheel. 
But as I was recovering from my mastectomy, I made a surprising discovery: going flat was freeing! It made me feel like my original self again—that flat-chested feisty pre-teen who was brave and focused and believed anything was possible. That girl who wrote poetry and stories and plays about heroines before boobs and boys and patriarchal expectations took up permanent space in her head.
So now, I am obsessed with having this conversation—how to live joyfully after going flat—with a fascinating array of women. Women who have made the shift to flat—even when it wasn’t their first choice—and discovered their unique brand of joy, meaning and fulfillment on the other side.

description:
God & the Gavel explores the collision of religious liberty, justice, and power in American life. Hosted by Professor Marci Hamilton — Professor of constitutional law at the University of Pennsylvania, founder of CHILD USA, former clerk to Justice Sandra Day O’Connor, and a leading voice on child sex abuse issues, the First Amendment, and extreme religious liberty — and Dr. Leslie Griffin, Boyd Professor of Law at  UNLV Law School, a scholar of law and religion, Catholic theology, and bioethics, the show examines the collision of faith and science, child sex abuse cases, the Supreme Court, and the rise of Christian Nationalism. 


Speaking from the perspective of progressive believers, humanists, and nonbelievers alike, we challenge the idea that authoritarianism and faith must go hand in hand. Each episode highlights Americans choosing conscience over control, accountability over cover-up, rights over authoritarianism, science over ignorance, and pluralism over power — because real religious liberty protects everyone, not just the loudest voice in the room.

Entre Más Humana, Más Diosa es un podcast para volver a ti.

Soy Susana Franco y creé este espacio para acompañarte a reconocer la mujer GranDiosa que ya eres, mirar con honestidad lo que hoy te limita y atreverte a caminar hacia tu siguiente nivel.

Aquí hablamos de lo luminoso, pero también de lo incómodo: de nuestras heridas, emociones, miedos, decisiones, relaciones, cuerpo, energía, autoexigencia, límites y de esas partes de nosotras que muchas veces preferimos esconder.

Porque para mí, ser GranDiosa no significa ser perfecta. Significa tener la valentía de aceptarte, hacerte responsable de ti, escuchar tu propia verdad y tomar acción.

En cada episodio encontrarás conversaciones honestas, reflexiones, prácticas, canalizaciones y herramientas como el Detox Energético para ayudarte a salir del ruido, conectar con tu brújula interior y vivir con mayor presencia, placer y privilegio.

Yo no estoy aquí porque tenga todo resuelto. También estoy aprendiendo a ser humana. Y quizá esa sea la verdadera magia de este camino: entender que nuestra vulnerabilidad no nos quita poder, nos acerca a él.

Porque cuando tú cambias, no cambias solamente tú. Se transforman tus relaciones, tu entorno y la manera en la que impactas a quienes te rodean.

Entre Más Humana, Más Diosa.
Entre más tú, más GranDiosa.

title: Salt of the Earth
author: Luis
description:
Welcome to Salt of the Earth. This is a Christian podcast built around one verse, Matthew 5:13, where Jesus tells a crowd of ordinary people, you are the salt of the earth. Not try to be. Not aim to be. He says it like a fact.

Back then, salt was valuable. It preserved food before there were refrigerators, it brought out flavor, and it was even used as pay. That is actually where the word salary comes from. Salt worked quietly and changed everything around it just by being there.

But salt can also lose its flavor. It can still look like salt while the substance is gone. That is what this show is about: how we live as salt, and how we get our flavor back when we feel like we have lost it.

This one is for believers, and for anyone who feels like they have lost their salt and want it back. We will have honest conversations, and I cannot wait for you to meet the guests we are bringing in. So stay salty, my friends. 

This is Salt of the Earth.

After the Lights Turn Off is a scripted horror anthology for listeners aged nine and up — and for the adults who never stopped sleeping with one foot outside the covers.

Every week, host Kimmy Lantern takes you somewhere that shouldn't be occupied. A fog bell ringing on a dead clockwork in 1922. An abandoned drive-in where the concession stand starts up at midnight with the power cut at the pole. A drained swimming pool in the middle of the Blizzard of '78, where the night man keeps writing in the log that he can hear somebody doing laps.

These stories are built on real things. Real machinery, real history, real science — daytimer radio licenses, saltpeter mines, pneumatic cash tubes, four-hundred-year-old irrigation ditches. When you find out how a thing actually worked, the ghost gets worse.

And there are rules. Every episode, a kid notices something the adults missed and lives because of it — and the rule they used is a real one. Don't run from a big cat. Reach, don't go. You're allowed to say no.

No gore. No cruelty. The animal always makes it out. That's a promise, and we've never broken it.

Twelve episodes. One season. And a door at the end of Kimmy's hallway that she keeps saying she'll explain.

New episodes weekly. Bring your flashlight.

Family Friendly. (Recommended for ages 8+)

description:
What does grief sound like when it’s spoken out loud?

Monsanto and Yvette Dávila—two mothers bound by grief after the deaths of their children, Siwe (15) and Dasan (26)—the podcast centers honesty over closure and presence over answers.
Rooted in faith, culture, and lived experience, the show explores grief in its many forms: child loss, identity shifts, estrangement, rage, remembrance, and renewal. Through storytelling, guest voices, and ritual-inspired reflections, Dionne and Yvette create a sacred space where sorrow and joy are allowed to coexist.
This is not a guide to “getting through” grief. It’s a companion for sitting with it—where vulnerability is honored, healing is non-linear, and love continues beyond loss.

description:
Unlaced with Lacy

Girl talk, but the kind you have after the second glass of wine.

Unlaced is the space for risky sensuality, real femininity, and the conversations we usually only have behind closed doors. Hosted by Lacy — professional dancer, choreographer, and pole instructor — each episode dives into confidence, body image, kink exploration, and the freedom that comes with finally being seen.

Expect origin stories, unfiltered confidence check-ins, a sip-and-talk segment over whatever's in the glass that week, narrated original fantasy stories, spicy book talk, and real stories submitted by listeners just like you.

This is a safe, no-shame space to explore your sensuality on your own terms — no judgment, just realness.

New episodes drop biweekly. Submit your own story or question at the link in bio.

18+ — contains mature themes and sexual content.
